claim: Bernard & Thomas (1989): top-minus-bottom SUE decile hedge earned +4.19% abnormal over 60 trading days post-announcement, 7.74% after 180 days (1974-1986 sample); drift smaller in large firms.
Bernard & Thomas (1990): ~25-30% of PEAD occurs in the 3-day windows around the next quarters' announcements.

Martineau (2022, Critical Finance Review): analyst earnings surprises have not predicted 60-day post-announcement returns for all-but-microcap stocks since 2006 (microcaps since 2016); prices now fully react on announcement day.
Counter-claim (HHS thesis, 2026, not peer-reviewed): large-cap 60-day PEAD rose from 0.52% (2005-2020) to 1.99% (2021-2024); zero-cost hedge >8%/yr. Uses SUE + FF3 CAR; long-short, not long-only.

VERIFIED (UCLA Anderson Review 2026-01-21 on Subrahmanyam 2025, SSRN 5930255): replicating the announcement-RETURN-based earnings drift factor (Dickerson-Julliard-Mueller) on US stocks Feb-2001..Dec-2024: t=2.18 with all stocks, t=1.43 once microcaps are excluded. Hirshleifer-Peng-Wang (RFS 2025) t~14 drift also includes microcaps and isn't robust to size controls (per Subrahmanyam).

Frazzini & Lamont (NBER w13090): stocks expected to announce earnings in a month beat non-announcers by ~61 bp/month (~7%/yr, t>5), 1973-2004; premium concentrated in high-past-announcement-volume stocks; attributed to small-investor attention buying. Implies our 'no buy 2 days before earnings' rule may forgo a premium (but raises single-stock variance).

Novy-Marx (2013): gross profits/assets predicts returns about as well as B/M; among largest stocks profitability spread 26 bp/mo (t=1.88) vs value 14 bp/mo (t=0.95); the two are -0.58 correlated, 50/50 mix Sharpe 0.44 vs market 0.34. Long-short, annual rebalance.
Asness, Frazzini, Pedersen QMJ (RAS 2019): long-short quality earns 4-factor alpha ~60 bp/mo in US (t~10), positive in 23/24 countries; tends to do well in downturns (flight to quality).
NBER w33601 (Mar 2025): QMJ returns largely explained by profitability + PEAD; no significant alpha vs profitability alone (claim from search synthesis, not verified in full text).
Chan, Jegadeesh & Lakonishok (1996, JF): price momentum and earnings momentum (surprise, analyst revisions) each independently predict 6-12 month returns; analysts adjust slowly.

Chen et al. (2020, JBFA) 'post-forecast revision drift': analyst forecast revisions still predict returns; strongest for downgrades and for consistent (non-herding) revisions (from abstract synthesis).

Brandt, Kishore, Santa-Clara, Venkatachalam (2007): sorting on 3-day earnings announcement return (EAR) beats SUE (~6.3%/yr abnormal L/S); EAR returns concentrate around the next 4 announcements (~3.3% per 3-day window); EAR+SUE combined ~11%/yr. 1987-2004 sample, pre-decay.

S&P 500 Quality index vs S&P 500 total return: 2023 24.97 vs 26.29; 2024 25.70 vs 25.02; 2025 13.43 vs 17.88; 2026 YTD (to Sep) 13.11 vs 12.75. Momentum index 2024 46.01, 2025 26.86, 2026 YTD 27.84. Quality has roughly tracked, not beaten, cap-weight recently.
JP Morgan US Quality factor (Russell 1000 universe) lagged Russell 1000 in 2023 (25.1 vs 26.5), 2024 (21.2 vs 24.5), 2025 (11.9 vs 17.4); 5y ann 14.3 vs 14.1 (to 2026-01-30).

McLean & Pontiff (2016, JF): across 97 anomalies, long-short returns are 26% lower out-of-sample and 58% lower post-publication; decay larger for higher in-sample returns and for price-only signals. Haircut any paper number by >=50%.

Savor & Wilson (2016, JF): scheduled announcers earn ~9.9% annualized abnormal return; risk-based (announcements carry market-wide news). Ogneva/Xia/Ye (2024 WP, via search synthesis): broad US premium weaker after 2004 but still significant for the largest (top 100/500) firms - unverified in full text.

Guidance asymmetry: downward management guidance penalty is larger than the premium from then beating consensus (Accounting & Business Research 2011). Post-guidance drift is upward for both good and bad news guidance (JBFA 2012: overreaction to bad, underreaction to good).
optionsdatabase.com Q4-2025 earnings: of 1,968 beats, 835 (42%) still closed lower on the reaction session - 'a beat is not a trade'; avg abs reaction 7.04% across 3,189 optionable names.

IVolatility study of 9,651 S&P 500 earnings events (~5y): median implied move 4.14% vs realized 3.32%; up/down split 51.5/48.1; avg up +4.61%, down -4.58%. Earnings day is a coin flip with ~4% one-day move - larger than a 2xATR stop on many names.

Lopez-Lira & Tang (JFE 2026; data Oct 2021-May 2024, post-cutoff): GPT-4 headline scores predict next 1-2 day drift; long-short 34 bps/day pre-cost (overnight news), Sharpe 2.97 pre-cost; long leg only 8 bps/day (Sharpe 0.78) vs short leg 26 bps/day. Stronger in small stocks and negative news; authors say only low-cost traders (market makers) can exploit.
Lopez-Lira & Tang: LLM strategy returns decline as LLM adoption rises (price efficiency improving); predictive ability scales with model size (GPT-1/2/Llama2-7b ~none).

FINSABER (KDD 2026): over 2004-2024 and 100+ symbols, buy-and-hold significantly outperforms LLM timing agents FinMem and FinAgent in bias-controlled setups; neither has significant alpha (p>0.34). Prior reported LLM gains came from short windows / hand-picked popular stocks (survivorship, data snooping).

FINSABER regime analysis: LLM agents are too conservative in bull markets (lag passive) and too aggressive in bear markets (heavy losses); authors recommend trend detection + regime-aware risk controls over more framework complexity.

Glasserman & Lin (JFDS 2024): in-sample LLM news backtests carry look-ahead bias plus a 'distraction' effect from company knowledge; anonymizing company names improved in-sample returns, esp. large caps; out-of-sample difference mostly insignificant, borderline benefit for large caps.

Chan (2003, JFE): stocks with public news show momentum (strongest drift after BAD news, up to 12 months); extreme moves with NO identifiable news tend to reverse next month. Effects mainly in smaller, illiquid stocks; most bad-news drift is on the short side.

Lopez-Lira & Tang (GPT-4 headlines, post-cutoff): initial reaction ~90% predictable but not tradable; tradable 1-2 day drift has 55-58% hit rate, 0.34-0.50%/day L/S pre-cost; long leg only ~8 bp/day (Sharpe 0.78) vs short leg 26 bp (Sharpe 2.01); stronger in small stocks; Sharpe fell 6.54 (late 2021) -> 3.68 (2022) -> 2.33 (2023) as LLM adoption rose.

Lou, Polk & Skouras (2019, JFE): ~100% of momentum (price, earnings, industry) abnormal return accrues overnight (3F alpha 0.95%/mo overnight vs 0.11% intraday, 1993-2013), stronger in large-cap/high-price stocks; value/size and most other anomalies earn intraday. Implication: a momentum/news-continuation long bought at next-day 9:45am open forgoes the overnight leg.
Tetlock (2007, JF): high WSJ-column pessimism predicts next-day Dow decline (~8 bp per SD) that reverses over days 2-5 - media sentiment at market level is noise, not information.

Tetlock, Saar-Tsechansky & Macskassy (2008, JF): negative-word fraction in firm news (S&P 500, 1980-2004) predicts lower earnings and ~3.2 bp lower next-day returns per SD; only real-time DJNS (not morning WSJ recaps) predicts; costs likely erase it; fundamentals-focused stories matter most.

Glasserman & Lin (2023, JFDS): LLM news-sentiment backtests suffer look-ahead bias AND a 'distraction effect' (model's prior knowledge of the firm distorts judgment, worst for large caps). Anonymizing company names in headlines improved in-sample returns and borderline out-of-sample for large firms.
Barber & Odean (2008, RFS): individual investors are net buyers of attention-grabbing stocks (news, abnormal volume, extreme 1-day moves); those purchases subsequently underperform.

Barber, Huang, Odean & Schwarz (2022, JF) Robinhood herding: top-0.5% user-surge stocks (4,884 events) average +14% on herding day, then about -3.5% abnormal over 5 days and ~-5% over a month; extreme surges (900 events) +42% then -6.4% (5d), ~-9% (1m).
Greenwood & Sammon 'Disappearing Index Effect' (JF 2025): S&P 500 addition abnormal return fell from ~7.4-7.6% (1990s) to ~0.8-1.0% (2010s); deletions ~-0.6%.

Counter-claim (ETF Trends/ETF Stream, 2025): index inclusion effect 'came back' with retail; 2025 S&P 500 additions averaged ~7.4% announcement-day outperformance. Announcement is usually after the close, so most is in the next-open gap - unverified whether post-open drift remains.

Lopez-Lira, Tang & Zhu 'Memorization Problem' (arXiv 2504.14765, v. 2026-08-11): GPT-4o recalls pre-cutoff S&P 500 daily levels with 0.61% MAPE and 80.6% directional accuracy; post-cutoff MAPE 16.9%, direction 45.7% (no skill). Prompting 'pretend it's date X' and masking do not reliably prevent recall -> any LLM backtest on pre-cutoff data is invalid.

Alpha Arena S1 (nof1, live, $10k each, crypto perps, 2025-10-18..11-03): 4 of 6 frontier LLMs lost 42-59% (GPT-5 -58.7%, Grok 4 -57.9%); win rates 25-30%; nof1 says early PnL was dominated by fees from over-trading. Leveraged crypto, 2 weeks: not transferable except as a warning on overtrading.

Alpha Arena S1.5 (2025-11-19..12-03, US equities incl. TSLA/NVDA/MSFT/AMZN/GOOGL/PLTR/NDX): 'Mystery Model' (Grok 4.20) won with +12.11% aggregate; 2-week sample, no index-relative significance reported.

StockBench (arXiv 2510.02209): 20 Dow stocks, daily decisions, 2025-03-03..06-30; equal-weight buy-and-hold +0.4% (maxDD -15.2%); best agent Kimi-K2 +1.9% (maxDD -11.8%). Most agents beat B&H on return and drawdown, but margins are small over a 4-month window.

LiveTradeBench (UIUC, arXiv 2511.03628): 21 LLMs, 50 live trading days (Aug-Oct 2025) on US stocks + Polymarket; best stock returns GPT-4.1 +6.25% (Sharpe 2.64), o3 +6.04%; general LLM benchmark scores and reasoning models did not predict trading performance; stock skill did not transfer to Polymarket where most models lost. No SPY-relative comparison found in paper (unverified vs index).

AIEQ (Amplify AI Powered Equity ETF, live since 2017, IBM Watson-based stock picking): annualized total return 9.60% vs S&P 500 14.73% since inception through 2025-09-30 -> longest live AI stock-picker record trails the index by ~5 pts/yr.

Verified from AIEQ annual shareholder report (as of 2025-09-30): AIEQ NAV avg annual return 1y 19.68% / 5y 8.71% / since 2017-10-17 9.60% vs S&P 500 TR 17.60% / 16.47% / 14.73%. One good year does not fix a 5y gap of ~7.8 pts/yr.

sec-api.io event study, 8-K Item 4.02 (non-reliance/restatement), 2007-2023 ex-2021, n~1,700: mean CAR vs SPY -1.10% (t+1), -1.54% (t+5), -2.00% (t+20); median -2.64% at t+20; 64% filed after 4pm. Negative news keeps drifting for weeks -> exit/avoid, never 'buy the dip'.

8-K item codes alone explain ~15% of reaction-size variation; Item 8.01 aggregate ~0 but content (trials, M&A, regulatory) highly reactive; event-specific tags matter more than item numbers (arXiv 2607.08346, via search synthesis - full text fetch timed out, unverified).

Free source stack: SEC EDGAR (no key, <=10 req/s with declared User-Agent; RSS by form/CIK; full-text search since 2001 at efts.sec.gov); Finnhub free tier company-news REST 60 calls/min (websocket news is paid); Alpha Vantage NEWS_SENTIMENT (free-key limits vary).

M&A: targets jump toward but below offer; acquirers often fall, especially stock deals, partly from arb shorting that later rebounds (Mitchell-Pulvino-Stafford 'Price pressure around mergers'). Long target after announcement = merger-arb payoff: small capped upside, large downside on deal break - poor fit for a beat-SPY $1k book.

Analyst recommendation changes: immediate price move but little/no post-change drift in 2003-2010 (JFE 2016 'Can analysts pick stocks for the long run?', via synthesis); intraday evidence shows much of the apparent day-0 move precedes the public time stamp. Don't chase upgrades the next morning.

Buyback anomaly mixed: Fu & Huang (Mgmt Sci 2016) find no long-run abnormal returns after repurchase announcements in 2003-2012; others find it persists mainly in small, volatile, undervalued firms. Not a large-cap edge.

Cohen, Malloy & Pomorski (JF 2012): long-short on 'opportunistic' insider trades earns 82 bps/month value-weighted (180 bps EW) abnormal; 'routine' insiders (same month each year) earn ~0. Filter routine trades out before using Form 4.

Lakonishok & Lee (RFS 2001): insider-trade informativeness concentrated in smaller firms; insider purchases (not sales) carry the signal. Later Nordic studies (2022-2024 samples, theses, C-grade) find little large-cap response.

Hong, Li, Ni, Scheinkman & Yan (NBER w21166): days-to-cover (short ratio / turnover) beats short ratio; 1988-2012 EW low-minus-high DTC decile spread 1.19%/month (t=6.67), VW 0.67%/month. Long-only use: avoid top-DTC names (crowded shorts = negative expected drift).
Greenwood & Sammon (JF 2025): S&P 500 addition abnormal return fell from ~7.4% (1990s) to ~0.8% (2010s) -> do not trade inclusion announcements.
Fu, Huang & Lin (Mgmt Sci 2016): positive long-run drift after open-market buyback announcements (pre-2003) disappears in 2003-2012 (4,652 events). Buyback announcements alone are not an edge.

Brown, Davies & Ringgenberg (RoF 2021): ETF creation/redemption flows reveal non-fundamental demand; high-flow ETFs subsequently underperform low-flow ETFs (1.1-2.0%/month long-short). Long-only: don't chase ETFs with record inflows.

Boehmer, Jones, Zhang & Zhang (JF 2021): net marketable retail buying predicts next-week outperformance ~10 bps/week cross-sectionally; 2024 replication (SSRN 4703056) finds weaker effect in 2016-2021, esp. large caps, and sensitivity to retail-ID method.

Cohen, Polk & Silli 'Best Ideas': managers' highest-conviction picks outperform (~2.8-4.5%/yr in updated work). Systematic 13F hedge-fund cloning (Jivraj WP, 2004-2019): 14.14%/yr vs S&P 10.34% with 47-day lag; Faber: 45-day delay costs ~1.5%/yr. Working papers, survivorship risk.

CFTC COT for S&P 500 futures: predictive value weak and mixed; signals unreliable once weekly reporting delay is accounted for (J. Intl Fin Mkts 2013); at most ~1-week speculator continuation. Not useful for a daily long-only stock picker.
Practitioner (X @bigearningsai, 2026-08-09): 'buying every fantastic earnings beat returned 17% over 2023-2026; SPY returned 37% in the same window.' Method unpublished - unverified.
Practitioner (X @thekilldigest, 2026-10-12): large-cap PEAD design ~0.56% gross per trade; same design on S&P 400/600 drifted LESS (contradicts 'small caps drift more'). Unverified backtest.

Speed: large-cap prices react to earnings news within milliseconds; most post-announcement opportunity gone in ~2 seconds (UCSD Rady 2025 summary); ~25% of an article's information priced in 5 seconds with news analytics (Fed IFDP 1233). An LLM reading news minutes-to-hours later has zero speed edge; any edge must come from interpretation over days.

Cooper, Cliff & Gulen (2008): SPY Feb-1993 to Dec-2006, $1 in close-to-open returns grew to $6.54 while open-to-close fell to $0.61 (pre-cost). Later analyses say the gap persisted but weakened after 2022 (unverified).
Grégoire & Martineau (2022, JAR) 'How is earnings news transmitted to stock prices?': S&P 500 quotes adjust almost immediately to earnings news, including after-hours.

'So Many Jumps, So Few News' (NBER w32746): most large stock price jumps have no identifiable news (from title/abstract; unverified detail) - consistent with Chan (2003) that no-news moves tend to revert.

FINRA Reg SHO daily short VOLUME files (cdn.finra.org/equity/regsho/daily/CNMSshvol<YYYYMMDD>.txt) are not short interest: ~40-50% of volume is routinely marked short by market makers; don't read high daily short-volume ratio as bearish positioning (unverified magnitude; practitioner consensus).

Kim, Muhn & Nikolaev (Chicago Booth WP, arXiv 2407.17866): GPT-4 with chain-of-thought on anonymized financial statements predicts next-year earnings direction 60.35% vs 52.71% for median analyst; EW long-short Sharpe 3.36 (~10%/yr alpha), but value-weighted results favor a plain ANN. Sample is largely pre-cutoff -> memorization caveat (L-006). Working paper.

TradingAgents (arXiv 2412.20138) reports +26.62% on AAPL in Jan-Mar 2024 vs +2.05% best baseline; an independent GitHub reproduction got -25.44% for the same window and alleged 2025 news leakage into the 2024 backtest; repo now disclaims reproducibility. Single-stock, 3-month agent backtests are not evidence.

Jensen, Kelly & Pedersen (2023, JF): ~82% of 153 factors replicate after Bayesian multiple-testing adjustment, across 93 countries; but factor returns decay ~47% post-publication. Counter to pure 'replication crisis' - factors are real but smaller.

Jiang, Li & Wang (2021, JFE): splitting returns into news vs non-news (15-min intraday + overnight, Dow Jones Newswire): news-driven returns continue for several days without reversal; non-news returns reverse. 1-week long-short on news returns 1.60-3.34%/mo gross, 1.37-2.10%/mo net of costs. Supports N-001 with modern data; long-short.

FINSABER (Li, Kim, Cucuringu, Ma; KDD 2026, arXiv 2505.07078): 2004-2024 rolling windows on historical S&P 500 incl. delisted, long-only: buy-and-hold significantly beats FinMem and FinAgent (paired t-test p<=0.012 in all composite setups); neither LLM agent has significant CAPM alpha (all p>0.34); FinMem overtrades (commission ratio 5-9x FinAgent); LLMs Sharpe 0.12/-0.19 in bulls vs buy-and-hold 0.61; no active strategy beat buy-and-hold Sharpe in bull years. Authors: regime-aware risk control and trend detection matter more than model scale.
arXiv 2510.26228 (2025): long-only LLM news strategy positive out-of-sample from Jan 2024 but short test, weakly significant alpha (via synthesis; unverified).

Vendor/practitioner revisions claims: Zacks Rank top stocks 'nearly tripled' S&P 500 since 1988; a 1993-2022 S&P 500 backtest of 3-month estimate revisions 16.3%/yr vs 10.4% index (Sovereign Investor); AAII 2000-2016 screen positive. Marketing/unaudited - grade C.

Fed FEDS 2024-049: aggregate S&P 500 analyst forecast errors are predictable from macro nowcasts, and near-term aggregate revisions relate to 3-6 month index returns (via synthesis; unverified details). Market-level, not stock selection.

Berkman, Koch, Tuttle & Zhang (2012, JFQA) 'Paying attention: overnight returns and the hidden cost of buying at the open': high-attention stocks (big prior-day moves/news) show elevated overnight returns (retail opening buy pressure) that reverse intraday. Buying attention names at the open systematically overpays.

Counter-evidence to N-003: RFS 2026 'Evidence from Day and Night Signals' (via synthesis) finds conventional momentum accrues intraday through 2019 and overnight-signal momentum lacks significant alpha; Lachance (2023, RFE) finds overnight momentum profits attenuate over 5 years. Overnight-vs-intraday momentum location is CONTESTED - don't build a rule on it.

Bradshaw/Kothari et al. survey (Annual Review of Financial Economics 2016, 'Analysts' forecasts and asset pricing'): documents underreaction to forecast revisions; JFE 2016 finds recommendation-change drift insignificant in 2003-2010. Revisions evidence for large caps post-2010 remains thin - unverified.
Cross-sectional momentum: past 3-12m winners beat losers over 3-12m holds (NYSE/AMEX 1965-89; 12m/3m ~1.31%/mo long-short); partly reverses in yrs 2-3. Jegadeesh-Titman JF 1993.
Momentum long side contributes ~as much as short side; significant in large caps (weaker than small). Asness et al. JPM 2014.
Live-trade cost data 1998-2011: value & momentum survive trading costs at scale; short-term reversal does not. Frazzini-Israel-Moskowitz AQR 2012.
Time-series momentum: own past-12m return predicts next month in all 58 futures markets; partial reversal after ~1y. MOP JFE 2012.
Momentum crashes are partly forecastable: after market declines with high vol, during rebounds; dynamic version ~doubles Sharpe. Daniel-Moskowitz JFE 2016.
Vol-scaled momentum nearly doubles Sharpe and virtually eliminates crashes (in-sample). Barroso-Santa-Clara JFE 2015.
Nearness to 52-week high dominates past returns in predicting returns; no long-run reversal. George-Hwang JF 2004.
Recency of 52-week high roughly doubles the strategy's monthly return (US 1965-2008). Bhootra-Hur JBF 2013.
One-month reversal: extreme deciles on 1m lagged return differ ~1.99%/mo 1934-87; 12m lag positive. Jegadeesh JF 1990.
10-month SMA timing on S&P 500 TR 1901-2012: 10.2% vs 9.3% gross, vol 12.0% vs 17.9%, maxDD -50.3% vs -83.5% (no costs/taxes). Faber JWM 2007/2013 update.
MA and trading-range-break rules on Dow 1897-1986: buy signals beat sell signals; sell-signal returns negative. Brock-Lakonishok-LeBaron JF 1992.
With FDR data-snooping control on DJIA 1897-2011, best technical rules not selectable ex ante; in-sample gains offset by low transaction costs. Bajgrowicz-Scaillet JFE 2012.
Survey of 95 technical-analysis studies: 56 positive/20 negative/19 mixed, but undermined by data snooping and cost/risk handling. Park-Irwin JES 2007.
RSI/MACD index studies show some profits after 1% costs in Italy/Canada/Dow, none in Nikkei; no snooping correction. Chong-Ng-Liew JRFM 2014.
High past volume = glamour-like, lower future returns; high-volume winners reverse faster. Lee-Swaminathan JF 2000.
Low-vs-high volatility decile alpha spread ~12%/yr globally 1986-2006; not explained by size/value. Blitz-van Vliet JPM 2007.
Betting-against-beta: low-beta earns higher risk-adjusted return; factor is leveraged long-short. Frazzini-Pedersen JFE 2014.
97 predictors: returns 26% lower out-of-sample, 58% lower post-publication; bigger decay for price/volume-only signals. McLean-Pontiff JF 2016.
New factors should clear t>3.0 given multiple testing; many published findings likely false. Harvey-Liu-Zhu RFS 2016.
Robinhood daily bars to 2026-10-21: SPY ATR14 0.91% (2xATR 1.82%), +6.4% vs 200DMA, 1y vol 12.8%; QQQ ATR14 1.50% (2xATR 3.01%), +7.2% vs 200DMA, 1y vol 19.8%. Uptrend regime.
SPIVA YE2025: active large-cap funds trailing S&P 500: 1y 78.8%, 3y 66.8%, 5y 89.0%, 10y 85.6%, 15y 89.9%, 20y 92.9%.
SPIVA mid-year 2026: 67% of active large-cap funds trailed S&P 500 in H1 2026.
Highest-turnover households netted 11.4%/yr vs 18.5% lowest-turnover vs 17.9% market (1991-96); gap from trading costs. Barber-Odean JF 2000.
Under 1% of Taiwan day traders reliably profitable net of fees. Barber-Lee-Liu-Odean JFM 2014.
Inverse-variance scaling of factors gives alphas/higher Sharpe (in-sample spanning). Moreira-Muir JF 2017.
Implementable out-of-sample vol-managed portfolios generally have lower Sharpe/CER than unmanaged. Cederburg et al. JFE 2020.
Stop-losses reduce expected return under random walk; can add value with momentum/regime-switching. Kaminski-Lo JFM 2014.
Individual stocks 1970-2005: stops neither reduce nor increase losses vs buy-and-hold; value is risk reduction. Lei-Li 2009.
10% stop on momentum 1926-2013 cut worst month from -49.8% to -11.4% (EW), >2x Sharpe. Han-Zhou-Zhu SSRN.
No peer-reviewed test of ATR-multiple stops found; practitioner tests say tight ATR trailing stops hurt.
Stop orders become market orders when triggered; fills can deviate significantly; noise can trigger them. SEC bulletin upd. 2026-08-18.
Full Kelly: huge volatile bets, severe drawdowns, very sensitive to mean-estimate error; fractional Kelly reduces risk. MacLean-Thorp-Ziemba.
Disposition effect: investors sell winners more readily than losers (PGR/PLR>1.5). Odean JF 1998.
Best ~4% of CRSP stocks created all net market wealth; most stocks lag T-bills; concentrated portfolios often lag. Bessembinder JFE 2018.
85k simultaneous identical market orders, 5 brokers: round-trip cost 0.07%-0.46% ex-commission; PFOF does not explain dispersion. Schwarz et al. JF 2025.
SEC 2020: Robinhood's high PFOF contributed to inferior prices costing customers $34.1M net of commission savings (2015-18); $65M penalty.
Market orders: price not guaranteed; limit orders: price guaranteed, fill not. SEC bulletin.
Robinhood fractional: $1 min; dollar orders execute immediately at market during RTH; handled Not Held; NMS only; no cancel 9:20-9:30.
Intraday spreads U/reverse-J shaped, widest in first 30 min after open (NYSE 1989). McInish-Wood JF 1992.
Closing auctions ~9% of US equity volume on a typical 2025 day, ~20% on rebalance/expiry days (vendor).
US stock/ETF settlement T+1 since 2024-05-28.
Cash account: selling a security bought with unsettled proceeds before settlement = freeriding, 90-day freeze. SEC bulletin upd. 2026-08-07.
FINRA Notice 26-10: PDT rules/$25k minimum replaced by intraday margin standards (margin accounts), effective 2026-06-04, phase-in to 2027-10-20.
Gains on assets held <=1y taxed as ordinary income; >1y at 0/15/20%; $3,000/yr net loss deduction. IRS Topic 409.
Wash sale window is 30 days before or after the loss sale; disallowed loss added to replacement basis. IRS Pub 550.

VERIFIED (Ogneva, Xia & Ye, Mar 2024 WP, p.7): long announcers/short non-announcers weekly hedge, 1991-2022: full-sample premium gone after 2004 (not positive since 2011, consistent with Heitz et al. 2020), but largest-500 announcers still earn FF5+momentum alpha ~0.30%/week (~16.7% annualized), largest-100 ~0.23-0.25%/week; significant. Per-event: ~+0.3% expected vs ~4.6% typical single-name earnings move (F-019) => tiny edge per bet, needs many names.

Junk crash: Goldman non-profitable tech basket -19% in 2021 and -57% in 2022 vs Nasdaq-100 -32% (Yahoo/Bloomberg); profitless companies fell >64% Feb-2021 peak to Dec-2022 (Morningstar). Unprofitable firms are only ~4.1% of Russell 1000 cap (end-2021), so a junk filter rarely binds for >$10B names but avoids the worst tail.
Lopez-Lira & Tang v6 (verified in text): ChatGPT overnight-news strategy annualized Sharpe fell 6.54 (2021Q4) -> 3.68 (2022) -> 2.33 (2023) -> 1.22 (Jan-May 2024). Clear decay as LLMs spread.

Lopez-Lira & Tang v6 (verified): with 20 bps transaction costs the daily-rebalanced overnight-news strategy Sharpe goes 2.97 -> -0.39 (mean daily 0.34% -> -0.04%); 25%-rebalance version 2.89 -> -0.21. Retail-cost daily news trading has no edge.

Lopez-Lira & Tang v6: excluding price<=$5 and below-20th-pct NYSE cap stocks, pre-cost long-short still >300% cumulative over sample -> predictability is not purely micro-cap. (Search-summary claim that 'large caps show no drift' is UNVERIFIED and contradicted here; still long-short and pre-cost.)

Pelster & Val (Finance Research Letters 2024): GPT-4 with live web search rated S&P 500 stocks' attractiveness; ratings correlated positively with subsequent earnings surprises and returns and updated promptly after news. Short live window (2023); effect size per strategy not verified here.

Heitz, Narayanamoorthy & Zekhnini (2020, 'The disappearing earnings announcement premium'): US announcement premium vanished after the 2004 8-K disclosure reform (timely 8-Ks resolve uncertainty before earnings). Counter to F-006/F-016; reconciled by F-026 (survives only in the largest ~500 firms).

Retail flow nuance: aggregate retail order imbalance (Boehmer, Jones, Zhang & Zhang 2021, JF) positively predicts returns over weeks, but Robinhood herding / attention surges predict reversals (N-008). The negative signal is the *surge* in attention, not retail buying per se.

He, Lv, Manela & Wu 'Chronologically Consistent LLMs' (JFE 2026): ChronoBERT/ChronoGPT point-in-time checkpoints 1999-2024; in a news->next-day-return task they match Llama 3.1's Sharpe, implying look-ahead bias in that specific news-return application is modest. Counterweight to L-006: memorization ruins numeric/forecast backtests more than headline sentiment backtests.

AI-managed ETFs: FINQ's AI-run ETFs reported beating S&P 500 over a few months in 2026 (no bear-market test); practitioner 5-year review found no AI-quant ETF beat SPY CAGR. Blog/press, unverified numbers.

Novy-Marx (2015, NBER w20984): earnings surprises (fundamental momentum) subsume price momentum in cross-sectional regressions; price momentum has no alpha vs earnings momentum. But since PEAD is weak in large caps post-2006 (F-003, F-005), this suggests large-cap momentum itself may be weaker than headline numbers - check vs Trader's technicals.

Hossain (2010 WP via CXO): post-SOX (2-business-day Form 4 filing), 2-day CAR from filing date is +1.13% for insider purchases vs +0.32% pre-SOX (41,603 filings 2003-2009); higher-ranked insiders (CEO/CFO) more informative; size effect not significant. Much of the move is on filing day, hard to capture at a next-morning cadence.

S&P 500 insider purchases 2021-2023 (newsletter study): beat S&P 500 by 3.7 pts over 1 week and ~2.5 pts over 1-3 months but lagged by 2 pts at 6 months and 6.5 pts at 1 year; a 2003-2022 thesis finds strongest after-cost returns at 1-5 day horizons. Unverified, low-quality sources; consistent with short-lived large-cap signal.

Counter-evidence to FP-003: short-interest predictability has weakened through 2023 (dissertation), arbitrage/hedging shorts dilute the signal, and one thesis finds high short interest in large caps associated with higher (not lower) future returns. Cross-sectional SI signal survives mainly in small/illiquid/opaque firms. Mostly non-peer-reviewed.

Hanno Lustig (Substack, 2025): Robinhood customers' aggregate annualized return ~3.7% vs S&P 500 16.8% from 2020-Q2 through 2025-Q1 (via synthesis; unverified detail). Base rate: the crowd on our own platform badly lags the index.

Alpha Arena (nof1.ai) Season 1, live crypto perps, 2 weeks ending ~2025-12-03: Qwen3 Max +22.3%, DeepSeek +4.9%, Claude Sonnet 4.5 -30.8%, Grok 4 -45.3%, Gemini 2.5 Pro -56.7%, GPT-5 -62.7% (iweaver summary). 2 weeks, leverage, crypto - no evidence of durable LLM skill; dispersion shows how much luck dominates short windows like our paper period.

Rapach, Ringgenberg & Zhou (JFE 2016): AGGREGATE short interest is a strong predictor of lower US market excess returns (1 s.d. higher SI ~ 6-7 pts lower annualized; annual OOS R^2 13.24%). Usable as a slow monthly regime input (de-risk toward cash/index when aggregate SI spikes), not a daily signal.

Counter-evidence to FP-006: sector-ETF flows predict positive returns for ~1 month, then negative in months 2-3 (small regional journal); aggregate unexpected equity-ETF flows co-move with but don't predict returns (Dannhauser WP). Flow reversal is a multi-week effect, not next-day.

Chen, Kelly & Xiu 'Expected Returns and LLMs' (SSRN 4416687): LLM news embeddings beat bag-of-words/Word2Vec for cross-sectional return prediction, incl. after costs; edge strongest for full articles and complex/negated text; predictability persists days in small stocks but fades quickly in large stocks; international LLM long-short Sharpe ~1.16-2.37 across 16 markets.

FinanceBench (Islam et al. 2023): GPT-4-Turbo with retrieval answered only 19% of 150 filing-based questions correctly (13% wrong, 68% refused); with the right evidence pages in context accuracy rose to ~85%. Numbers pulled by an LLM from filings need a verbatim source check.

Cohen, Malloy & Nguyen 'Lazy Prices' (2020, JF): firms that substantially change 10-K/10-Q language YoY underperform non-changers; VW long non-changers/short changers 34-58 bp/month over the next year; risk-factor-section changes up to 188 bp/month; no announcement-day reaction, returns accrue over 6-18 months; not a small-cap effect (short-side firms avg $3.5B). An LLM can diff filings cheaply.

Lazy Prices post-publication: student GitHub replication (2020-2024) finds most-similar consecutive 10-Ks had strongest long-term returns but non-monotonic across bins; 2022 replication on 2000-2018 positive. Weak/unaudited out-of-sample evidence.

Earnings-call tone: Price, Doran, Peterson & Bliss (2012, JBF) find call tone (esp. Q&A) predicts 60-day abnormal returns/PEAD; 2023 ICAIF study on S&P 500 finds contextual embeddings help predict PEAD but raw text sentiment hurt after 2020; recent work says call sentiment mostly drives immediate (day-0) returns.

Faber (2007/2013): S&P 500 TR held only when month-end price > 10-month SMA (else T-bills), 1901-2012: CAGR 10.18% vs 9.32% buy-and-hold; max drawdown 42.24% vs 83.66%; in market ~70% of time, <1 round trip/yr; underperforms in about half of years. Gains come from avoiding big bears, not from beating the index in normal years. Pre-cost/tax.

Lucca & Moench (2015, JF): SPX +49 bp on average in the 24h before scheduled FOMC announcements (1994-2011), ~80% of annual excess return. Kurov et al. (PMC 2020): drift disappeared after 2015 (9.2 bp 2016-2019, not different from non-announcement days); HHS thesis: SPX pre-FOMC 0.323 -> 0.055 post-publication.

Cederburg, O'Doherty, Wang & Yan (2020, JFE): across 103 equity strategies, volatility-managed versions beat unmanaged in only 53 vs 50 cases; real-time out-of-sample versions generally earn LOWER Sharpe than unmanaged, due to unstable spanning regressions. Barroso & Detzel: don't survive costs. Vol-targeting is not an alpha source for us.

VIX futures backwardation (spot > futures) has been followed by POSITIVE S&P 500 returns, stronger at quarterly horizon; contango has no signal (Fassas & Hourvouliades, JRFM 2019; adj R2 0.01-0.035). Panic regimes are contrarian buy zones on average, not sell signals.

Gilchrist & Zakrajsek (2012, AER): excess bond premium (EBP) carries nearly all credit-spread predictive power for activity; 1-SD (~20 bp) EBP shock -> stock market ~-7 pp vs trend; Fed note: +50 bp GZ spread raises 12-month recession probability ~7 pp. Fed publishes EBP monthly (lagged). Recession/drawdown warning, not a daily signal.

Diercks, Katz & Wright (Fed FEDS 2026-010 / NBER w34702): Kalshi macro markets give well-calibrated, fast-updating density forecasts; fed funds forecast MAE ~1.0 bp (same as fed funds futures), median/mode 0 bp on FOMC days 2022-2025; headline CPI median MAE 6.3 bp vs Bloomberg consensus 8.1 bp; core CPI comparable.

Burgi, Deng & Whelan (UCD WP 2025 / CEPR DP20631), 300k+ Kalshi contracts: prices informative and sharpen near close, but strong favourite-longshot bias: contracts <10c lose >60% after fees, >50c earn small positive returns; takers average -31.46%, makers -9.64%. Read cheap-tail odds (<10c) as overstated.

Polymarket calibration: thesis on 113,135 resolved markets (2023-01..2026-04) 30-day Brier 0.045, calibration slope 0.95-0.98, small +0.9-1.6 pt Yes bias; independent analysis of 61,518 markets (traded prices) finds slope 0.98-0.99 within a week, ~0.92 at 2-3 months, thin markets too extreme (0.86-0.91), ~15% of a week's price move reverses (overreaction). Number of traders predicts accuracy; lifetime volume barely does.

Rasooly & Rozzi (arXiv 2503.03312) field experiment on 817 markets: random price shocks remain visible up to 60 days but fade; markets with more traders, volume and an external probability anchor are harder to manipulate. Low-trader markets can be pushed.

Ng, Peng, Tao & Zhou (2025, via thesis): in the 2024 election identical Polymarket and Kalshi contracts traded ~3c apart persistently (>$2M arb in 15 days); Polymarket led price discovery when relatively more liquid. Cross-check both venues before trusting a level.

Snowberg, Wolfers & Zitzewitz (QJE 2007): election-night prediction-market swings map causally into asset prices; Republican presidential win raised equity valuations ~2-3% (and post-1980 10y yields ~13 bp). Method: delta(asset) / delta(probability) gives the market's priced sensitivity.

Sanity backtest (biased: current S&P100, 2014-2026, 0.30% RT): stock>200DMA adds nothing (26.5% vs 28.7% CAGR); SPY<200DMA->cash cuts CAGR to 16.9%; weekly worse than monthly; momentum beats EW-all-members control (18.5%) by 8-10 pts, mostly hindsight per T-021.

Novy-Marx & Velikov (RFS 2016): buy/hold spread is the best cost mitigation; 2/3 less trading frequency cuts turnover only ~1/3; >50%/mo turnover anomalies rarely survive costs. Our test: top10-in/rank>20-out cuts turnover 688%->418%/yr, similar CAGR.

Sanity backtest stops on momentum book: none 26.5% CAGR/-36.9% DD; 2xATR/-8% (current rule) 8.9%/-34.4% with 3x turnover; 3xATR/-10% 11.9%; 5xATR/-20% 21.4%/-27.8%. Tight stops cost ~15 pts/yr with little DD benefit.
Breakers bind often: days >8% below peak SPY 17%, QQQ 22%, momentum book 36%; >2% loss days/yr SPY 7.9, momentum 22.7. 8% pause must mean no new buys + review, not liquidation.
Moskowitz & Grinblatt (JF 1999): industry momentum explains much of stock momentum; momentum books carry concentrated sector risk.
Sanity backtest sector cap <=3 per GICS sector: vol 27.7%->24.0%, Sharpe 0.99->1.05, CAGR -1.7 pts; <=2: vol 22.3%, CAGR -2.6 pts (today's sectors, look-ahead).

Earnings announcement premium: Frazzini-Lamont 2007 (7-18%/yr strategies, strong in large caps, ~20 days); Savor-Wilson JF 2016 (9.9% annualized for announcers); Barber et al JFE 2013 (9 of 20 countries). Avoiding earnings forgoes a small premium.

Earnings days ~11% of annual return variance for large caps (SMU WP) and ~16.7% of annual vol in 2017 vs 3% in 1990 (Sammon) on ~1.6% of days. No study tests an N-day pre-earnings no-entry rule; 2 days is judgment.

Retail limit orders (Rev. Finance 2026, 30(2):459): fill 65.2% vs 99.8% marketable; non-fill opportunity cost ~15.9 bp, yet all-in shortfall ~8 bp lower than marketable (via synthesis; full text not opened).
Linnainmaa (JF 2010): retail limit orders are picked off (adverse selection), mechanically producing poor post-trade returns; use marketable limits, not resting ones.
Rebalance frequency: weekly vs monthly in sanity backtest raised turnover 688%->1717%/yr and cut CAGR 26.5%->21.3%; monthly + hold buffer best for small account (with Novy-Marx-Velikov 2016).

Aboody, Lehavy & Trueman (2010, RAST; UCLA WP 2008): stocks with the strongest prior-12-month returns earn +1.58% market-adjusted in the 5 trading days BEFORE earnings and -1.86% in the 5 days AFTER; significant after transaction costs; linked to individual-investor attention, not information.

Nguyen (2026, JBFA): stocks with the highest past earnings-announcement max return (EA_MAXRET) beat the lowest by 85 bp risk-adjusted (107 bp market-adjusted top decile) in the 10 days before announcements, 1981-2020 - lottery demand. Swedish 2015-2025 thesis: modest pre-EA premium concentrated in last 3 days, then reversal.

Trueman, Wong & Zhang (2003, JAE): internet stocks 1998-2000 ran up into earnings and through the next open (+4.9% buy 5 days pre to next open), then intraday reversal on day+1 (-3.1% open-to-close after +1.6% overnight). Older NYSE studies found pre-EA run-ups <1/10 that size, only on day -1/0. Bubble-era sample.

IV crush is irrelevant to a stock-only holder: the post-earnings implied-vol drop changes option prices, not the stock's expected return; what matters is the realized move vs our stop. Large-cap implied moves ~ realized on average (M-017), so the implied move is a fair estimate of earnings-day risk for sizing (reasoning from M-017; no direct study).

LLM call/guidance tone: ICAIF'23 (S&P 500 point-in-time, 2010-2022): ChatGPT-derived contextual call features add 53-354 bp per trade over an earnings+fundamentals baseline OOS (long-short), while raw textual features alone degraded results; Gong, Li & Zhang (SSRN 4950924): GPT-4o-measured positive facts/tone predict positive OVERNIGHT returns (i.e. mostly day-0); Tilburg thesis: GPT-4o sentiment beats Loughran-McDonald, Q&A more predictive than prepared remarks.

Simply holding the market except early recession earns about the same (0.18%/month).

Moskowitz & Grinblatt (1999, JF): industry momentum (buy past-winning industries) is strong and explains much of individual-stock momentum; strongest at 1-month formation/holding in their sample (detail from memory - unverified). Long-short, pre-publication.

VIX below mean).

BUT own SPY test 2016-2026: Nov-Apr +0.062%/day vs May-Oct +0.061% (t=0.02); QQQ +0.073% vs +0.087%. Recent US large-cap evidence: no effect. Momentum decline kink: Hanauer/Lin et al. (NBER w28624): US stock momentum factor fell from 0.92%/month (1987-Jun 2002) to 0.16%/month after; industry and factor momentum show the same post-2002 kink, partly attributed to the 2002 Morningstar rating reform. 'Better Opt Out' (2024 WP, review by BagelQuant): combined options-implied stock-selection signal (CPIV, dP-dC, dO/S, RVIV, vol-of-vol) VW long-short Sharpe 1.18 (1996-2008) -> 0.16 (2008-2021), FF6 alpha 11.40% -> 1.56% (insignificant); much pre-2008 'alpha' was a timestamp look-ahead (OptionMetrics quotes after 4pm close until Mar 2008). For long-only large caps the signal is mostly irrelevant; its main use is flagging hard-to-borrow, crowded-short names to avoid.

Does EARLY vs LATE attention timing predict 10-day drift after good earnings news in small/mid caps? Proxy test (tools/attention_drift_test.py): 150 random CURRENT $0.3-10B names (seed 20261022), EDGAR 8-K 2.02 events 2021-10..2026-10, n=2,405; attention proxied by volume (Barber-Odean): pre5 = pre-news 5d volume / baseline, run5 = pre-news return. Good news (reaction-day ≥+5% vs IWM), n=543: 10d drift vs IWM mean +0.84%, median -0.23%, t 1.40. EARLY proxy (pre5 <1.3, run5 <10%), n=341: +0.69% (t 0.85), median -0.69%. LATE proxy (pre5 ≥2 or run5 ≥25%), n=35: +0.07%, median -2.33%, hit rate 34%. Reaction-day volume terciles: low 2.3x → +1.08%, high 3.7x → +0.56% (sign matches DellaVigna-Pollet inattention drift; t<1.2). MA-R4 rerun excluding the 5 biggest-drift tickers (ABCL, FDMT, QBTS, SGMT, SYRE): good news +0.10%, EARLY -0.38% (t -0.6), LATE -0.85% (median -2.33%). Verdict: no measurable 10-day edge from buying EARLY. The only consistent hint is LATE = worse median / hit rate, matching S-002/N-007/N-024, but n=35 and t≈0. Use attention timing as a VETO (skip LATE names), not as a buy trigger. Caveats: survivorship (current constituents); event dates cluster (t overstated); volume is not X/ST attention. [Replication, 14:00 ET: a second independent sample (seed 7, 150 names, 2,433 events) gives good news +0.60%, EARLY +0.55% (ex top-5 +0.16%, t 0.3), LATE +2.75% (ex top-5 +2.48%, n=26, t 0.9). The LATE hint does NOT replicate; it flipped sign. Seed 1 week-clustered t: good news 0.75, EARLY -0.36, LATE 0.10. Final: on a volume proxy, neither EARLY nor LATE timing predicts 10-day drift in small/mid caps. The LATE veto rests only on the literature (S-002 Robinhood herding, N-024 open-price overpayment, A-grade) and costs little to keep. EARLY is not an edge, so it needs its own catalyst thesis.]
